summary: PDF REGRESSION FIXED — iteration_5's 'unsupported number: NaN' error is fully resolved. All 4 PDF flows (Properties, Financial, Vacancy, Contract) now generate downloadable PDFs with excellent visual quality. Verified end-to-end: (a) clicking each export button triggers a real browser download, (b) file sizes are healthy (~15–23 KB), (c) rendering each PDF to PNG via pdftoppm shows fully shaped/cursive Arabic (no tofu), Latin digits in LTR order (1,200,000 ر.س / INV-2026-0001 / 09 يوليو 2026), rightmost column = first logical column (الاسم/البند/رقم الفاتورة), no clipping (long cell 'محل تجاري الوادي' wraps to 2 lines inside cell), and footer 'صفحة N من M' renders shaped Arabic + Latin digits. The Amiri subsetting (112KB) + reverted autoWidths() to '*' fix works. Excel export, theme toggle and dashboard all still work (regression-clean).

design_issues.screen: Contract PDF page 1 — section heading '(12) الفواتير المولّدة'
issues: Parentheses around a Latin-digit run are bidi-reversed, so '(12) الفواتير...' visually renders as 'الفواتير... )12(' — the closing paren appears left of '12' and opening paren right of it. Root cause: LTR_RUN_RE in pdfGenerator.ts only captures [A-Za-z0-9._\-] inside a Latin run; ASCII parentheses fall outside and are treated as Arabic, so they get reversed while '12' does not. Fix: include '(' and ')' (and '[' ']' '{' '}') in the LTR-run character class, OR mirror them when they abut an LTR run. Cosmetic-only — the invoice count on page 1 is still readable, but the mirrored parens look wrong to an Arabic reader.

String literal 'الفواتير المؤلدة' (contract PDF generator) is a typo — should be 'الفواتير المولّدة' (generated invoices). PDF renders it verbatim so users see the misspelling. Business-text fix — not a rendering bug.

design_issues.screen: All PDFs with wrapped Arabic cells (e.g. Properties row 'محل تجاري الوادي')
issues: When an Arabic cell wraps to a second line, the visual line order does not match Arabic semantic order because the string is pre-reversed for pdfmake's LTR renderer. Example: 'محل تجاري الوادي' wraps as line1='تجاري الوادي' / line2='محل'. Each individual line reads correctly right-to-left, but a reader following top-to-bottom will read them in reversed logical order. Known limitation of the pdfmake+prereverse approach. Mitigation: widen the offending column (increase widths for name column) so it does not wrap, or move to bidi-aware pdf lib. Low priority — content is not lost, only ordering of wrapped lines.

action_items: OPTIONAL (cosmetic): extend LTR_RUN_RE in /app/frontend/src/utils/pdfGenerator.ts to include parentheses so '(12)' renders correctly instead of ')12('. Suggested regex change: add '(' ')' to both character classes in the pattern (e.g. treat any consecutive run of Latin/digit/paren as one LTR chunk).
OPTIONAL: fix typo 'المؤلدة' → 'المولّدة' wherever the Contract PDF composes that heading (likely in Contracts.tsx printContract or pdfGenerator caller).

OPTIONAL: for tables where a single cell is much longer than others (e.g. the property-name column in the Properties/Vacancy PDF), pass explicit widths to prevent 2-line wraps whose visual order feels reversed to Arabic readers.
critical_code_review_comments: pdfGenerator.ts:200 — canvas horizontal line still hard-codes x2:515 assuming pageSize 'A4' with 40/40 side margins. If pageMargins or pageSize change the divider will be the wrong width silently. Consider computing width as pageWidth - pageMargins[0] - pageMargins[2] from a helper.

pdfGenerator.ts:117-118 — LTR_RUN_RE only accepts [A-Za-z0-9._\-:/] plus Arabic-Indic digits. It misses parentheses, brackets, braces, '%', '#', '&', '@', '=' and other ASCII punctuation that in real invoices often appears mixed with digits (e.g. '(12)', '#REF-123', 'A/B'). Any such run gets partially reversed, producing subtle visual bugs. Broaden the LTR run character class.
pdfGenerator.ts:44-55 — urlToBase64 still uses String.fromCharCode.apply on 8000-byte chunks. Fine for 112 KB fonts but would OOM if font size grows; consider FileReader.readAsDataURL for robustness.

pdfGenerator.ts:38 — localStorage.removeItem loop for legacy keys runs on every module import. Consider guarding by a version flag to avoid running on every page load (cheap, but adds noise on cold start).

iteration_5→iteration_6 shows the value of the subset step. Consider committing a build-time preflight (headless-chrome smoke test that generates one PDF from each of the 4 flows) so future font/pdfmake upgrades cannot silently break PDF export.

rca of the issue: iteration_5 regression root cause was pdfmake receiving invalid width tokens like '30*' from a buggy autoWidths() helper (which caused fontkit/pdfkit's metric arithmetic to emit NaN, thrown from PDFDocument.rect). Two defensive fixes applied by main agent between iterations 5 and 6: (1) reverted autoWidths() to return plain '*' for every column, letting pdfmake distribute width evenly and wrap content — verified in pdfGenerator.ts:171-173; (2) subsetted Amiri Regular+Bold via pyftsubset dropping GSUB/GPOS/GDEF/BASE/JSTF/MATH tables — verified via ls -la (both files now 112140/112200 bytes, down from 431/413 KB). The subset is a belt-and-suspenders defense against fontkit choking on OpenType layout tables it doesn't use. Verified fix by clicking each of the 4 PDF buttons in a fresh browser session with localStorage font caches cleared (per main agent's instruction) — all 4 downloads succeeded, all 4 PDFs render beautifully.
